author: Peach Tree Times
title: Gov. Kemp announces $26 million for Georgia transportation and airport projects
text:
Governor Brian P. Kemp and the State Road and Tollway Authority Board of Directors approved $26 million in funding on June 9 for Georgia Transportation Infrastructure Bank grants and low-interest loans to support 20 roadway projects and two regional airport hangar projects across the state.
Kemp said, “These awards are on top of the historic funding we’ve put toward local transportation projects in recent years, and today’s announcement further represents our commitment to investing in high-quality infrastructure, including in our rural areas. We’re taking a long-term view with this funding, which is why for the first time, GTIB is extending awards to two regional airports to construct multiple hangars, supporting business aviation and driving economic activity.”
The State Road and Tollway Authority also announced that applications are now open for FY 2027 GTIB grants and loans. Community Improvement Districts as well as local, regional, state government entities, and publicly owned airports are eligible to apply for infrastructure improvements such as roadways or airport hangars.
Jannine Miller, Executive Director of SRTA, said, “GTIB continues to accelerate critical local transportation projects that improve safety, strengthen connectivity, and expand economic opportunities across Georgia. Communities of all sizes, rural areas, CIDs, and airports can leverage GTIB’s grants and low-interest loans to move projects forward faster and close funding gaps. Thanks to the $46 million AFY 2025 budget enhancement from Governor Kemp and the General Assembly, this record-level funding remains available to help communities build key infrastructure to thrive.”
Since its creation in 2010 by SRTA—a state-level authority operating tolled facilities within Georgia—GTIB has provided $272 million in loans and grants supporting more than $1.3 billion worth of statewide transportation improvement projects through capital investments only. The program evaluates applications based on benefits such as mobility improvements or economic value; an advisory committee reviews recommendations before final approval by the board.
According to the official website of the Government of Georgia’s executive branch—which operates from Atlanta’s Governor’s Mansion—the governor’s authority extends statewide across all counties, serving residents through various initiatives including international outreach since establishing a representation office in Japan in 1973, according to the official website.
